item.title: Planet Money: How surveillance crept up on us
item.description:
For years, police have spent billions of tax dollars on watching us, tracking us, and recording us. In the largest police department in the country, these surveillance systems were paid for and adopted without the kind of public oversight cities usually require. 

In the wake of 9/11, the New York Police Department built one of the most sophisticated and omnipresent surveillance systems in the country. 

And while decisions were being made about what tech to adopt and how much to pay for it, few outside the NYPD were consulted. Not the City Council nor the public. For over a decade, the only paper trail of these purchases were offline, stored in filing cabinets, inaccessible to the public. 

Today on the show, how the country’s largest police department built its surveillance system, and the fight to get police everywhere to tell us how they’re watching us.

item.description:

In 2007, Bruce Robison’s robot submarine stumbled across an octopus settling in to brood her eggs. It seemed like a small moment, but as he went back to visit her month after month, what began as a simple act of motherhood became a heroic feat that has never been equaled by any known species on Earth.

item.title: The Automation Ladies: From Computer Science To Manufacturing Software With Ignition with Mia Skertich
item.description:
A lot of people think you need a perfect plan to get into industrial automation. Mia Skurdic proves the opposite. She started college unsure of her direction, discovered programming for the first time in an intro engineering rotation, and later landed in the Ignition ecosystem almost by accident, then never looked back.

We dig into what it’s really like to grow inside the manufacturing world as a computer science major: building MES solutions as a systems integrator, connecting Ignition to ERP systems, and learning why the database layer often carries the “real” business logic. Mia also gives a clear, practical breakdown of Perspective vs Vision and MES vs SCADA, including how OEE, traceability, and process orchestration change the conversation beyond simple real-time machine visibility.

Then we zoom out to the skills that make automation engineers dangerous in the best way: reading the manual, using the forums, learning by doing, and leaning on a community that actually shows up. We also talk AI as a lightweight troubleshooting partner, why vibe coding can make debugging harder, and the future trend Mia wants to see everywhere in OT: better software engineering practices like Git version control and repeatable deployments. We wrap with a reminder that you don’t have to be “a math genius” to build a great career, plus why Ignition Maker Edition is a legit way to learn through personal projects.

item.title: NerdWallet's Smart Money Podcast: How to Budget Money Your Way and Save Smarter for Big Milestones
item.description:
Learn how to pick a budget that fits your life, where to save for a big goal and how identity theft has changed.
Does a budget work without sorting your spending into needs and wants? And where could you keep money you’re saving for a big expense that’s five years away? Hosts Sean Pyles, CFP®, and Elizabeth Ayoola answer two listener questions. The first comes from a listener who splits her budget into monthly and one-time expenses instead of using the 50/30/20 rule. The second comes from a parent saving $13,000 for her daughter’s quinceañera whose CD is about to mature. 
Then, how has the identity theft playbook changed over 40 years, and what new risks could AI agents bring to your finances? Senior news writer Anna Helhoski talks with Eva Velasquez, CEO of the Identity Theft Resource Center. They discuss why there’s almost no barrier left to committing fraud, and why victims often feel ashamed even when they did nothing wrong. They also cover who pays when an AI agent makes a costly mistake for you, how freezing your credit has gotten easier, and why help for victims after the fact still falls short.

item.title: Filmspotting: Zuck Dynasty, Pt. 1 — The Social Network
item.description:
Aaron Sorkin has said his new The Social Reckoning is not a sequel so much as a companion piece to David Fincher’s The Social Network, which Sorkin also scripted. Whatever you call it, though, these two films are undeniably linked, not just by Sorkin’s involvement, but especially by their interest in the tech-bro enigma that is Facebook founder Mark Zuckerberg. So this week we’re returning to 2010 and The Social Network to consider how the film’s depiction of Facebook’s then-recent origin story plays from our social-media-saturated present; how Sorkin’s script and Jesse Eisenberg’s performance as Zuckerberg find humanity, and maybe even sympathy, in a pointedly unlikable protagonist; and how Fincher made it all work on screen, from the instant-classic Facemash montage to a final shot we’ll be forever refreshing in our minds. Then in Feedback, a longtime friend of the show shares some thoughts prompted by our recent episode on William Friedkin’s Sorcerer.

item.title: Planet Money: We try to fix election polling (update)
item.description:
Polling is facing an existential crisis. People aren't picking up the phone. Nobody wants to talk to pollsters. Trust is on the line. We pluck a solution from the economics canon and convince a polling firm to let us test it. 

Today on the show, we head to Marist College — home of the Marist Poll — to learn how to be pollsters ourselves. We learn the great moments in polling history, the latest science of polling, and find out all the tricks that pollsters use to get people to finish their surveys. Then we get on the phone and give it a try ourselves. And offer some of our own solutions. 

This episode was originally published before the 2022 midterm elections. 

We have an update on our idea to save polling, which Marist is still testing, and we find out what it might be able to tell us about the 2026 midterms.

item.title: Manufacturing Happy Hour: 307: Building the Factory of the Future - LIVE from Revere Electric's Executive Forum at UWM's Connected Systems Institute (Milwaukee, WI)
item.description:
Manufacturing has been collecting skills for centuries, and the list keeps growing.

Chris takes Manufacturing Happy Hour to Revere Electric’s Executive Forum at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee (UWM) for a live conversation about what the factory of the future needs in the plant and in the workforce. Joining him are Michael Cvelbar and Phil Bush of Rockwell Automation, Joe Hamann of the Connected Systems Institute (CSI), and Ryan Schneeberger of Revere Electric Supply.

Joe and Phil look at how new people get job-ready through student hackathons and a veteran training program. Ryan and Michael cover the other side, keeping people on the floor and giving operators more to do once they’re there. Students learn where AI adds value, while manufacturers want to see the return before they invest. And a room full of manufacturers toasts every time they say “digital twin.”

In this episode, find out:

  • Why Michael says manufacturers need backup plans when disruption hits
  • How Rockwell is preparing operators to troubleshoot their own equipment
  • Why manufacturers say new engineering graduates can take years to reach full productivity
  • How Rockwell’s Academy of Advanced Manufacturing trains military veterans as controls technicians
  • What flexible automation can do for a customer and why manufacturers stay cautious on AI until the ROI is clear
  • How Phil, Joe, Ryan and Michael describe their factory of the future when the audience asks

item.title: NerdWallet's Smart Money Podcast: Afraid to Ask for a Raise? Negotiate Your Salary With 5 Simple Words
item.description:
Learn how to get past the fear of negotiating for higher pay, even when your employer might say no.
Why does negotiating feel so scary, and how do you get past that fear? Hosts Sean Pyles, CFP®, and Elizabeth Ayoola talk with Kwame Christian, a negotiation expert, CEO of the American Negotiation Institute and host of the “Big Swings Only” podcast. They discuss how the fear of rejection, awkwardness and damaged relationships can keep you from asking for what you want, the everyday situations where you could negotiate more than you expect, and Kwame’s three-step framework for tough conversations. You’ll also hear what an “internal negotiation” with yourself looks like, how shifting from a fear of failure to a fear of regret could change your approach, and why staying quiet can turn into resentment.
And what do you do when the job offer seems final or your company says it doesn’t negotiate pay? Kwame walks Sean and Elizabeth through why it can help to think about total compensation instead of salary alone, the five-word question that could reveal room to move in an offer, how outside offers may give you leverage with your current employer, and how to respond to a “no negotiation” policy without attacking it. They also get into anchoring, why repeating the other side’s number can work against you, when raising your voice could backfire, and how to turn everyday negotiations into deliberate practice.
